faq: What does this tool calculate?
The difference in local clock time between two zones or places for a given date — with each side's DST state applied for that date.
Do I need an account?
No — pair in, difference out.
Can I use the result for professional work?
Yes for scheduling and planning; it applies the tz database's rules, the same foundation calendars use.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — places are chosen, never detected.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Zones resolve through the tz database and open geocoding; other tools may apply older rule vintages and differ during freshly changed rules.
Why isn't the difference constant?
Daylight saving — regions change on different dates or not at all, so gaps breathe by an hour through the year. Any source quoting one eternal number is quoting a season.
Half-hour differences?
Real and handled — India, Iran historically, parts of Australia: gaps like 5:30 and 3:30 are normal arithmetic here.
Ahead or behind?
The converter shows rendered times when direction matters; the difference alone is symmetric, geography is not.
The date line pairs?
Some pairs differ by more than 12 hours of clock while being 'one day apart'. The computation reports clock difference; the calendar consequence shows in the converter.
Why do some pairs never change?
When both sides keep identical DST behaviour (or neither observes), the gap is constant — New York–Los Angeles among the stable classics.
Ships and flights use what?
Aviation and maritime run on UTC internally and local at the edges — the difference this page computes is the local-facing one passengers live by.
